excerpt: Orderful is a cloud EDI platform that connects suppliers with retailers and logistics partners. Plans from $99 a month. Funding, who it suits and alternatives.
content:
Orderful is a modern, cloud-based EDI (electronic data interchange) platform. EDI is the decades-old standard that retailers, distributors, manufacturers and logistics companies use to exchange purchase orders, invoices, shipping notices and other documents. Orderful offers an API and connectors to business systems such as ERPs, onboarding of trading partners, validation against each partner's rules, and tools such as retail-compliant UCC-128 shipping labels, with the aim of making EDI faster to set up and easier to fix when something breaks.

Founder and CEO Erik Kiser started Orderful in 2017, FreightWaves reported. In 2021 Orderful announced a $19 million Series B led by GLP Capital Partners, with Andreessen Horowitz and Initialized Capital, saying it brought total funding above $32 million and would expand its EDI network and its sales and engineering teams. In December 2024 it announced a further $15 million growth round led by NewRoad Capital Partners.

Orderful publishes its prices. Shipping labels start at $99 a month, Web EDI fulfilment for businesses new to EDI costs $189 a month per trading partner, and the integrated API plan starts at $399 a month. Larger plans are quoted. It suits brands and suppliers that must trade electronically with big retailers such as those shown on its site, and logistics companies exchanging load tenders and status messages. It competes with SPS Commerce, TrueCommerce and Cleo, which also run large EDI networks.

We have not used Orderful for this page. It brings together Orderful's own website and the reporting linked under Sources, and says where each fact comes from. Nothing here is paid placement.
